title.suggested: Tom Allen arrives home after the Goss fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Weekly Dispatch reported that Allen arrived home in St. Louis from Cincinnati, unmarked after the Goss fight, and repeated that he would never again enter the ring.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The Weekly Dispatch: St. Louis, Thursday, September 21, 1876', page 5. Before 1878-12, so not the Post-Dispatch; the weekly edition of the Dispatch. 'This morning' suggests it first ran in the daily a few days earlier.

facts.fact: Allen returned to St. Louis by train from Cincinnati after the Goss fight and went to Tom Kelly's saloon at 9 North Ninth Street
places: Tom Kelly's saloon, 9 North Ninth Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen weighed about 180 pounds after the Goss fight
Allen repeated that he would never again enter the ring, saying that to win in the prize ring of the day a man must take his chances with thieves and duffers

notes: Allen's remarks are reported speech, not verbatim, so no quote is given. He also said Goss had hurried to New York and would soon sail for England.
